sentences.text: Jamninkaornis was a small passerine bird, a member of the suborder Tyranni that includes modern flycatchers and vireos.
The entire genus is represented by a single species, Jamninkaornis kencampbelli.
Our knowledge of the bird comes from just a right coracoid and humerus, the shoulder and upper wing bones, split across two rock slabs.
Jamninkaornis kencampbelli was formally described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Zbigniew M. Bochenski and colleagues.
The genus name combines the name of a local stream and valley with the Greek word for bird.
The bird lived in the Late Oligocene, specifically the Chattian age, about 26 million years ago.
Its fossils were recovered from Oligocene deposits in what is now Poland.
